hyps.why: Adding a 3x3 conv where the direct edge was absent opens a new path, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Turning on edge 5 with a conv adds a route into the output, gaining more than upgrading an existing op.
Activating edge 4 with a conv adds a deep path through node 1, a larger gain than swapping ops.
Edge 0 gates node 1, so replacing none with conv enables whole paths and gains substantially.
Replacing none on edge 1 activates a main route into node 2 and gives a large gain.
Removing a 3x3 conv on the direct edge costs more accuracy than removing a weak op.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 5 loses more capacity than deleting a skip or pool.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 4 removes a deep high-capacity path, a bigger drop than deleting weaker ops.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a parameter-free skip loses learnable capacity, a bigger drop than replacing weaker ops.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip on edge 5 drops capacity more than replacing weaker ops.
